newsitem.title: CHINA: China integrated silk group to calm industry.
newsitem.headline: China integrated silk group to calm industry.

text.p: China will this year move to calm its chaotic silk industry by creating a national integrated company to rear silkworms, process cocoons, weave thread and export silk products, officials and state media said on Friday.

The China Cocoon, Silk and Satin Group would be a force for reform of the ancient industry, which has suffered sharp swings in price and exports in recent years, the People's Daily quoted Vice Premier Li Lanqing as saying.

Creating a "one dragon" management system that combined production, processing and sales was the way to end structural divisions between farmers, mills and traders that had caused chaos in the industry, the newspaper quoted Li as saying.
An official of the state-owned China Silk Industry Co said his enterprise would be incorporated into the new integrated company.
"It will help macro-management," the official said.
The new group would be involved in every stage of the industry from mulberry tree planting to final exports, he said but declined to elaborate.
The People's Daily gave no details of the expected scale of the new silk group or how it would work with local firms.
Chinese state media said last year that 80 percent of silk enterprises were losing money and frustrated cocoon-raisers had chopped down about 30 percent of their mulberry trees.
China's cocoon output plunged 38 percent in 1996 to about 420,000 tonnes, with value of silk exports slumping to $2.5 billion from up to $3.5 billion in previous years, unofficial figures show.

The state-run Agricultural Bank of China had told all its branches to guarantee loans this year to cocoon-purchasing enterprises that were acting in line with government purchasing policy, the Financial News said on Friday.
The bank had decreed that no loans should be granted to enterprises that were not qualified or that raised prices arbitrarily or engaged in cutthroat competition, the newspaper said.
